recipes.title: Anzac Biscuits
recipes.description: Chewy, crisp oat and coconut biscuits sweetened with golden syrup, a classic Australian and New Zealand bake.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F).
Mix the plain flour, sugar, rolled oats and desiccated coconut in a bowl.
Melt the golden syrup and butter in a saucepan, then stir in the baking soda and water.
Mix the wet and dry ingredients together, adding a little more water if needed.
Roll the mixture into small balls and flatten them on baking trays.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden brown.

recipes.title: Flapjacks
recipes.description: Chewy British oat bars made with butter, brown sugar and golden syrup, baked in a tin and cut into oblongs.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F).
Heat the sugar, butter and golden syrup in a medium saucepan until the butter has melted.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the rolled oats.
Press the mixture over the base of a lightly greased 19 cm square baking tin.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 40 minutes.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then cut into oblong bars.
Leave until cold before lifting the flapjacks out, and store in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Scones
recipes.description: Light, golden British tea scones, served split with jam and cream.

ingredients.name: heavy cream, plus extra for brushing

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 230 °C (450 °F).
Pulse the plain flour, salt, baking powder and 2 tbsp of the caster sugar in a food processor. Add the butter and pulse to a cornmeal texture.
Add the egg and just enough heavy cream to make a slightly sticky dough.
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, knead once or twice and press into a 2 cm thick circle. Cut out 5 cm rounds.
Place the rounds on an ungreased baking sheet and reshape the leftover dough to cut more scones.
Brush the tops with a little cream and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.
Bake for 10 minutes, until golden brown.
Cool slightly and serve with fruit jam and extra cream.

recipes.title: Boxty (Irish Potato Cakes)
recipes.description: Irish griddled potato cakes made from grated raw and mashed potato with buttermilk and flour.

steps.instructionText: Wash, peel, chunk and boil half of the potatoes until soft.
Mash the boiled potatoes with the milk and 1 tbsp butter, and set aside.
Grate the other half of the potatoes (raw) into a strong cloth and squeeze out all the liquid.
Mix the grated potatoes, mashed potatoes, baking soda, buttermilk, plain flour and black pepper until well combined.
Warm a nonstick griddle or skillet over medium heat and melt some of the butter for frying.
Pour the batter on the griddle, 1/4 cup at a time, and fry until the edges are soft and the cake is bubbling.
Turn and cook the other side, then serve hot.

recipes.title: Dublin Coddle
recipes.description: Irish one-pot stew of sausages, bacon, potatoes and onions simmered slowly in stock.

steps.instructionText: Put the bacon, onions and sausages in a large pot and cover completely with the chicken stock.
Boil for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, cut into bite-sized pieces if needed, and bring back to the boil.
Simmer for 1 hour, until the potatoes start to disintegrate and thicken the broth.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with soda bread.

recipes.title: Colcannon
recipes.description: Irish mashed potato mixed with buttery cabbage and leeks, topped with melted Gouda.

steps.instructionText: Boil the potatoes until soft, drain, then shake them in a covered pot until they crumble.
Mash the potatoes with a fork. Season with salt, pepper, mace and paprika, then stir in the cream.
Add 100 g of the butter in pieces, cover and let it melt, then stir. Move the mash to a clean bowl.
Blanch the cabbage in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the leeks in the remaining butter for a few minutes, then toss in the cabbage for a few minutes more.
Mix the cabbage and leeks into the mashed potato.
Stir in most of the Gouda and sprinkle the rest on top.
Bake at 180 °C (350 °F) for 20 minutes, until the cheese has melted.

recipes.title: Corned Beef Pie
recipes.description: British double-crust pie filled with corned beef, mashed potato and onion; good hot or cold.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
Sift the flour into a bowl and rub in the lard and margarine.
Add just enough water to bind the mixture into a dough.
Roll out half the dough and line a large flan or quiche dish.
Boil the potatoes, drain, then mash with the butter.
Mix the chopped onion and the corned beef into the mash and spoon it into the lined dish.
Roll out the remaining dough, lay it over the dish as a lid and seal the edges.
Cut slits in the lid and brush with a little milk.
Bake for 40 minutes, until golden brown.

recipes.title: Coronation Chicken
recipes.description: Cold cooked chicken in a mild curry, apricot and mayonnaise sauce, created for the 1953 coronation.

steps.instructionText: Skin the cooked chicken and cut the meat into small pieces.
Warm the vegetable oil in a small saucepan and cook the onion gently until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the curry paste, tomato purée, red wine, bay leaf and lemon juice. Simmer uncovered until well reduced, then strain and cool.
Purée the apricot halves in a blender, then beat the cooled sauce and the apricot purée into the mayonnaise.
Whip the whipping cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the sauce.
Season with salt and pepper, adding a little more lemon juice if needed.
Fold in the chicken pieces and garnish with watercress.

recipes.title: Cornish Fairings
recipes.description: Crisp, ginger-spiced Cornish biscuits made with golden syrup.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F).
Sift the plain flour into a bowl and rub in the butter.
Sift in the caster sugar, baking powder, ginger, mixed spice and cinnamon, and mix well.
Stir in the golden syrup until the mixture forms a dough.
Roll the dough into walnut-sized balls and place them on a baking tray.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Cool for a few minutes on a rack before serving.

recipes.title: Irish Soda Bread
recipes.description: Yeast-free Irish loaf raised with baking soda and buttermilk, with a soft crumb.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F) and grease and flour a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
Combine the plain flour, baking powder, baking soda, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Blend the egg and buttermilk, then add them all at once to the flour mixture.
Mix just until moistened, as too much mixing makes the bread tough.
Stir in the melted butter and pour the batter into the pan.
Bake for 65-70 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean and the base sounds hollow when tapped.
Cool on a wire rack, then wrap in a tea towel for several hours or overnight for the best flavour.

recipes.title: Irish Stew
recipes.description: Traditional Irish stew of mutton, potatoes, onions and carrots, slow-cooked in a covered pot.

ingredients.name: mutton, deboned and cut in chunks

steps.instructionText: Choose a pot with a well-fitting lid and layer the potatoes, mutton, onions, carrots and parsley in it, starting and finishing with potatoes.
Pour in the water and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and cook over a very low heat for 2 1/2 hours, until the mutton is tender and the potatoes have thickened the liquid.

recipes.title: Jam Roly-Poly
recipes.description: Steamed suet pudding rolled around raspberry or plum jam and served with custard.

steps.instructionText: Stir the self-raising flour, vegetable suet, salt and lemon zest together.
Work to a firm dough with the lemon juice, egg and milk.
Roll out to a rectangle about 25 x 20 cm and spread the red jam to within 2.5 cm of the edges.
Roll up from a short end and seal the edges well with a little water.
Set the roll on a sheet of buttered foil and wrap it, sealing the ends well.
Set it in a steamer and steam for 2 hours.
Slice and serve with custard.

recipes.title: Lancashire Hotpot
recipes.description: Layers of lamb, onion and sliced potato baked slowly in a covered dish, an English northern classic.

steps.instructionText: Dice the lamb and set aside. Preheat the oven to 170 °C (325 °F).
Layer some of the potatoes in the bottom of a casserole dish and cover with a handful of the diced onions.
Add a layer of the lamb and sprinkle with the mixed herbs.
Repeat the layers until the dish is full, finishing with a layer of potatoes.
Pour in the boiling water to fill the dish.
Bake for at least 1 hour, until the lamb is tender.

recipes.title: Lancashire Parkin
recipes.description: Dark, sticky English gingerbread of oatmeal and golden syrup that softens as it is stored.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 150 °C (300 °F).
Mix the self-raising flour, oatmeal, caster sugar, ground ginger and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.
Warm the golden syrup gently in a saucepan without boiling, then melt in the hard margarine.
Line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Stir the hot syrup and margarine quickly into the dry ingredients.
Spread the mixture in the tray and bake on the bottom shelf for 2 hours.
Turn the slab out onto a cooling rack, then cut into four after 1 hour.
Store in a sealed tin for 48 hours to reach the correct sticky texture, then cut into strips.

recipes.title: Friar's Omelette
recipes.description: Scottish baked apple and egg pudding in a breadcrumb crust, turned out and dusted with sugar.

steps.instructionText: Peel, core and slice the apples and cook them in a saucepan with the water until soft.
Remove from the heat and stir in the butter, 50 g sugar and lemon juice. Leave to cool.
Mix the well-beaten eggs into the cooled apple mixture.
Butter a deep baking dish and press breadcrumbs onto the bottom and sides, keeping plenty for the top.
Pour in the apple mixture and cover with a thick layer of breadcrumbs.
Bake at 180 °C (350 °F) for 30 minutes.
Turn out onto a flat dish and sprinkle with the remaining sugar before serving.

recipes.title: Staffordshire Oatcakes
recipes.description: Thin yeasted oatmeal pancakes from Stoke-on-Trent, cooked on a griddle and filled with cheese or bacon.

ingredients.name: warm milk and water, mixed half and half

steps.instructionText: Mix the salt into the wholemeal flour and fine oatmeal.
Dissolve the fresh yeast in a little of the warm milk and water, add the sugar and leave until frothy.
Mix the dry ingredients with the yeast liquid and the rest of the milk and water to make a batter.
Cover the batter with a clean cloth and leave in a warm place for 1 hour.
Ladle enough batter onto a well-greased griddle to make an oatcake about 20 cm across. Holes will form as it cooks.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, until the top looks dry and the underside is golden.
Flip the oatcake and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes.

recipes.title: Pease Pudding
recipes.description: Northern English purée of yellow split peas cooked with a ham hock, spread on bread or served with ham.

steps.instructionText: Put the ham hock in a pressure cooker and cover with water.
Bring to full pressure, then lower the heat and cook for 30 minutes.
Release the pressure and take out the hock. Set it aside.
Add the split peas to the cooker, bring back to pressure and simmer as low as possible for 25 minutes.
Release the pressure, then tip the peas into a bowl with the butter and whisk until smooth.
Leave to cool, then serve on white bread, alone or with ham from the hock.

recipes.title: Queen of Puddings
recipes.description: English baked breadcrumb custard with a jam layer, topped with soft meringue.

steps.instructionText: Heat the milk, white sugar, lemon zest and butter until just below the boil.
Pour over the breadcrumbs and leave to cool slightly for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks and stir them into the breadcrumb mixture.
Bake at 180 °C (350 °F) for 35 minutes.
Let it cool a little, then spread the warmed raspberry jam carefully over the top.
Whip the egg whites with the vanilla sugar to soft peaks and spread the meringue over the jam.
Return to the oven for 15 minutes, until the meringue has browned.

recipes.title: Rhubarb Crumble
recipes.description: Tart stewed rhubarb under a buttery crumble topping, baked and served with custard.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan).
Rinse and drain the rhubarb, put it in a deep ovenproof dish and mix in the light brown sugar.
Rub the butter into the plain flour and wholemeal flour with your fingers until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Mix in the white granulated sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle the crumble over the rhubarb in a complete layer, without pressing it down.
Bake without a lid for 40 minutes, until crisp and a little brown.
Serve with custard.

recipes.title: Scottish Porridge
recipes.description: Creamy steel-cut oat porridge made with just oats, water and salt after an overnight soak.

steps.instructionText: Mix the steel-cut oats with the buckwheat flour in a bowl.
Add a splash of warm water and the lemon juice, cover and soak overnight, at least 7-8 hours.
Put the soaked oats, salt and the 375 ml water in a small pan and bring gently to a small boil, stirring, until it starts to thicken.
Turn the heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes, until the oats are tender.
Take off the heat and leave for 1-2 minutes before serving, with berries, nuts or yogurt on top.

recipes.title: Shortbread
recipes.description: Buttery, crumbly Scottish biscuit made from just flour, butter and sugar.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 140 °C (275 °F).
Cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Sift in the plain flour and salt and work into the butter and sugar until completely combined.
Shape the dough into a ball and roll out to 1.3 cm thick, chilling it briefly if it is hard to handle.
Cut into squares or rectangles and prick the tops with a fork in two parallel lines.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, until lightly browned.
Cool on a rack and store in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Shrewsbury Cakes
recipes.description: Soft, buttery little nutmeg biscuits from Shropshire, baked in minutes.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F) and grease two baking sheets.
Cream the butter and sugar in a large bowl until fluffy.
Stir in the egg white completely.
Add the nutmeg and plain flour and stir in completely.
Place teaspoons of the batter on the baking sheets, 5 cm apart.
Bake for 10 minutes.
If the cakes have stuck together, cut them apart with a knife, then lift onto a plate.

recipes.title: Steak and Ale Pie
recipes.description: Beef slow-simmered with onion, herbs and ale, topped with puff pastry and baked golden.

ingredients.name: fresh thyme, marjoram and parsley, chopped

steps.instructionText: Cut the beef into cubes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a saucepan and fry the onion, without letting it colour.
Add the beef and cook until medium brown, then stir in the plain flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, herbs, English mustard, bay leaf, salt and black pepper.
Slowly add the beef stock and ale and bring to the boil.
Simmer gently for 1 1/2 hours, until the beef is almost tender.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Skim off any fat, remove the bay leaf and adjust the seasoning.
Put the filling in a pie dish, cover with puff pastry and trim the edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, until the pastry is well risen and golden brown.

recipes.title: Stovies
recipes.description: Scottish stew of potatoes and onions slowly cooked in fat with leftover roast beef or lamb.

steps.instructionText: Peel the potatoes and slice them about 5 mm thick.
Heat the beef dripping in a large heavy pot with a tight lid and cook the onions until lightly brown.
Add the potatoes and stir well to coat them in the fat.
Cover and cook over very low heat, shaking the pot now and then, until the potatoes are cooked, about 40 minutes.
Add the cooked beef or lamb, mix through and turn up the heat to brown a little.
Season with salt, black pepper and nutmeg, and serve with the parsley.

recipes.title: Eton Mess
recipes.description: No-cook English dessert of strawberries, broken meringue and whipped cream with yogurt.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the strawberries, remove the tops and cut them in half.
Break the meringues into pieces, not too small, and put them in a bowl.
Whip the double cream with the vanilla essence and icing sugar until reasonably stiff.
Combine the whipped cream, Greek yoghurt, strawberries and meringues, taking care not to crush the meringue too much.
Serve in bowls.

recipes.title: Toad in the Hole
recipes.description: Sausages baked in a crisp, puffed Yorkshire pudding batter.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F).
Whisk the plain flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter.
Bake the sausages with the oil in a roasting pan for 10 minutes, so they cook and the pan gets hot.
Pour the cold batter into the hot pan; the oil should sizzle.
Bake for 40-45 minutes without opening the oven door, until risen and browned.
Serve hot.

recipes.title: Victoria Sponge
recipes.description: Classic English two-layer sponge cake sandwiched with jam and whipped cream.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F) and grease two 18 cm cake pans.
Cream the butter and caster sugar with a wooden spoon until softened.
Add the eggs, vanilla essence and self-raising flour and mix until smooth.
Divide the mixture between the two pans.
Bake for 20-30 minutes, until firm to the touch.
Cool completely on a rack.
Turn one cake upside down and spread with fruit jam and whipped cream, then top with the second cake.
Cut into wedges to serve.

recipes.title: Welsh Cakes
recipes.description: Little Welsh griddle cakes like flat scones, with currants and a golden crust.

steps.instructionText: Sift the plain flour into a large bowl and rub in the butter and salt until it looks like fine breadcrumbs.
Mix in the caster sugar and currants.
Beat in the eggs one at a time to form a thick dough, adding the milk if it will not come together.
Knead for 2-3 minutes until cohesive and slightly elastic.
Roll out the dough and cut 5-7 cm circles.
Heat a griddle on high, then lower to medium-low to stop burning.
Cook the cakes for 2-4 minutes on each side, until golden brown.

recipes.title: Welsh Rarebit
recipes.description: Rich cheddar and beer sauce poured over toast.

steps.instructionText: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over low heat and whisk in the plain flour.
Cook, whisking constantly, for 2-3 minutes without browning the flour.
Whisk in the Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt and black pepper until smooth.
Add the beer and whisk to combine, then pour in the double cream and whisk until smooth.
Gradually add the Cheddar cheese, stirring constantly, for 4-5 minutes until the sauce is smooth.
Pour the sauce over the toast and serve at once.

recipes.title: Bara Brith (Welsh Fruit Bread)
recipes.description: Yeasted Welsh loaf full of mixed dried fruit and spice, glazed with honey and served buttered.

steps.instructionText: Warm the milk until hand-hot, then mix it with 1 tsp of the brown sugar and the dried yeast. Leave for 15 minutes until frothy.
Sift the strong plain flour into a bowl with 50 g brown sugar and the salt. Rub in the butter, then stir in the mixed spice.
Add the egg and the frothy yeast, mix to a dough and knead on a floured surface until smooth and elastic.
Put the dough back in the bowl, cover and leave in a warm place to rise for 90 minutes.
Knock back the dough and knead again, slowly working in the mixed dried fruit.
Place the dough in a greased 900 g loaf tin and leave to rise for 35-40 minutes. Preheat the oven to 190 °C (375 °F).
Bake in the centre of the oven for 30 minutes.
Cover the tin with foil to stop it burning and bake for 30 minutes more.
Check the base sounds hollow when tapped. Brush the top with clear honey and cool on a wire rack.

recipes.title: Cullen Skink
recipes.description: Thick Scottish soup of smoked haddock, onion and mashed potato in milk.

steps.instructionText: Cover the smoked haddock with water in a shallow pan, skin side down.
Bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes, turning once.
Take out the fish, remove the skin and bones, flake the flesh and return it to the pan.
Add the onion, bay leaf, salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain the stock, discard the bay leaf and keep the fish warm.
Add the milk to the stock and bring to the boil, then stir in the mashed potato to make a rich, thick soup.
Return the fish and check the seasoning.
Serve with the butter added in small pieces and the parsley on top.

recipes.title: Fish Pie
recipes.description: English pie of poached salmon, smoked haddock and shellfish under creamy mashed potato.

steps.instructionText: Put all the fish and shellfish in a saucepan with enough milk to cover, then add the bay leaves and a pinch of salt.
Poach on low heat for 5 minutes.
Lift out the fish, skin the haddock and salmon, and flake them. Return to the milk and set aside.
Peel and boil the potatoes for at least 20 minutes, until soft, then mash very well with butter.
Beat in some of the poaching milk, the single cream and a little grated nutmeg to make a smooth mash.
Put the fish and remaining milk sauce in an ovenproof dish and pat it down gently.
Spread the mash over the top, ridge it with a fork and sprinkle with the Emmental cheese.
Bake at 220 °C (425 °F) for 30 minutes, until the topping is coloured and bubbling.

recipes.title: Bangers and Mash
recipes.description: Slow-fried pork sausages served with buttery mashed potatoes.

steps.instructionText: Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy frying pan over medium heat.
Add the sausages in a single layer and fry for 5 minutes, turning to colour them all over.
Turn the heat to low and fry gently for 25 minutes, turning every 5-10 minutes, until cooked through with no pink inside.
Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and chop them into pieces 1-2 cm thick.
Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, until soft enough for a knife to go in easily.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the pan off the heat.
Add the butter and milk and mash until smooth. Season with salt.
Serve the sausages on the mash.

recipes.title: Fish and Chips
recipes.description: Battered fried white fish with thick golden chips, served with lemon and vinegar.

steps.instructionText: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep fryer to 180 °C (350 °F).
Peel the potatoes, cut into thick wedges and deep-fry in batches for 6-8 minutes until crisp and golden.
Drain on kitchen paper, sprinkle with sea salt and keep warm.
Whisk the plain flour, corn flour and salt with enough cold water to make a batter.
Cut the fish fillets into thick slices and coat them in the batter.
Deep-fry the fish in batches for 5-6 minutes, then drain on kitchen paper.
Serve the fish and chips with the lemon wedges, parsley and a sprinkle of malt vinegar.

recipes.title: Lancashire Corned Beef Hash
recipes.description: Simple Lancashire stew of potatoes, onion and carrot with flaked corned beef stirred in at the end.

steps.instructionText: Put the potatoes, onion, carrot, tarragon, oregano, bay leaf, salt and white pepper in a large pan.
Add water until almost covering the ingredients, cover and bring to the boil.
Lower the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, until the potatoes soften.
If too wet, strain off some of the water.
Break up the corned beef and stir it in gently, then bring almost to the boil.
Switch off the heat and leave for 15 minutes.
Serve as it is, with buttered bread.
